extracted.intended_audience: Hospitals, hospital administrators, health system policymakers, CMS stakeholders, and prospective TEAM participants (notice-and-comment responders)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and commenting on CMS's proposed TEAM model rule provisions, including episode definitions and attribution, quality measure selection and baseline methodology, pricing and reconciliation, and risk adjustment and implementation timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation structure and glide path
rubrics_metrics.description: TEAM includes a 1-year glide path opportunity that allows TEAM participants to ease into full financial risk as well as three different participation tracks to accommodate different levels of financial risk and reward. Track 1 is an upside only risk track available for all TEAM participants in the first performance year and available to safety net hospitals for the first 3 performance years. Track 2 is a two-sided risk track that has lower financial risk and reward, relative to Track 3, and will be available to select TEAM participants in performance years 2 through 5. Track 3 is a two-sided risk track that has higher financial risk and reward, relative to Track 2, and is available to all TEAM participants in performance years 1 through 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains tracks' availability by performance year and for safety net hospitals; Track 1 provides no downside risk in PY1. Designed to accommodate different levels of financial risk and reward and to ease participants into downside risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode definition (clinical and time dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An episode has two significant dimensions: (1) a clinical dimension that describes which clinical conditions and associated services are included in the episode; and (2) a time dimension that describes the beginning and end of the episode, its length, and when the episode may be cancelled prior to the end of the episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under TEAM, episodes begin with an anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure identified by specific MS-DRGs or HCPCS codes and include all Medicare Parts A and B items and services during the anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure and a 30-day post-discharge period, with limited exclusions per regulation (42 CFR 512.525(d)-(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode inclusion and cancellation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An episode may be cancelled if the beneficiary (1) does not meet the beneficiary inclusion criteria, as outlined in 42 CFR 512.535; (2) dies during the anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure; or (3) the episode qualifies for the extreme and uncontrollable circumstances policy, as described in 42 CFR 512.537(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies three clearly enumerated conditions under which an episode is cancelled; inclusion criteria and extreme circumstances policy are referenced to specific regulatory sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode categories selection rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: TEAM tests five episode categories that represent high-expenditure, high-volume care delivered to Medicare beneficiaries and generally have a greater proportion of spending in the post-acute period relative to the anchor hospitalization or procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: these categories present greater opportunity to improve care transitions and reduce unnecessary hospitalizations and emergency care; chosen for scale and opportunity to achieve efficiencies in delivery and value-based care.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG updates and episode category conformity (spinal fusion example)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to add new MS-DRGs (523, 524, and 525) to the spinal fusion episode category starting Oct 1, 2026 and to update the spinal fusion definition at §512.505 to include these MS-DRGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: include proposed MS-DRGs so hospitals maintain sufficient episode volume, reflect current coding standards, ensure consistency with IPPS policies, and avoid evaluation challenges. CMS considered but is not proposing to leave MS-DRGs unchanged because that would reduce scale and not be responsive to policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode attribution when overlapping with CJR-X
rubrics_metrics.description: If a beneficiary in a CJR-X episode has a procedure performed at a TEAM hospital that would initiate a TEAM episode during the CJR-X 90-day post-discharge period, then that procedure would not initiate a TEAM episode or be attributed to the TEAM participant and the spending from that procedure would be included in the CJR-X episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the TEAM participant would not be attributed the episode, the procedure and associated spending would still be included in TEAM target price construction (used for average episode spending and trends). Policy rationale: hold the hospital where the anchor hospitalization/procedure occurred accountable and avoid duplicative calculations across similar models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality measure selection principles
rubrics_metrics.description: TEAM quality measures focus on care coordination, patient safety, and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and are aligned with measures used in existing CMS models and reporting programs wherever feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalized set of seven measures chosen for (1) alignment with TEAM goals, (2) hospitals' familiarity due to use in other CMS programs (IQR, OQR, HAC), and (3) alignment with CMS priorities (National Quality Strategy). Goal: minimize duplicate reporting and leverage existing reporting infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific TEAM quality measures (CQS inputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The measures are: Hybrid Hospital-Wide All-Cause Readmission (Hybrid HWR) (CMIT ID #356); CMS Patient Safety and Adverse Events Composite (CMS PSI-90) (CMIT ID #135) (claims-only in PY1); THA/TKA PRO-PM (CMIT ID #1618); Hospital Harm—Falls with Injury (CMIT ID #1518); Hospital Harm—Postoperative Respiratory Failure (CMIT ID #1788); Thirty-day Risk—Standardized Death Rate among Surgical Inpatients with Complications (ISCMR) (CMIT ID #134); Information Transfer PRO-PM (CMIT ID #1797) (for certain outpatient episodes in PY3-PY5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These seven measures will be used to calculate the Composite Quality Score (CQS), which will be combined with reconciliation amounts to tie quality performance to payment. Some measures transition from claims-only to hybrid methodology and have specific PY applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing reporting programs for quality data
rubrics_metrics.description: TEAM participants will not submit separate quality data to CMS for TEAM. Instead, CMS will utilize data already reported through established CMS quality reporting programs, eliminating duplicate reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligning with Hospital IQR, OQR, HAC programs where possible to reduce reporting burden and leverage validated data and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement performance period alignment for selected measures
rubrics_metrics.description: For Hospital Harm—Falls with Injury and Hospital Harm—Postoperative Respiratory Failure, CMS proposes alignment with the Hospital IQR Program's calendar year reporting requirements, utilizing a one-year measurement performance period. For ISCMR, CMS proposes alignment with the Hospital IQR Program's two-year rolling measurement performance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal aims to minimize participant confusion by aligning TEAM measurement periods with existing hospital reporting programs; CMS seeks comment on these proposed timeframes for PY2–PY5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sliding historical CQS baseline methodology (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the current fixed CQS baseline approach with a sliding historical CQS baseline methodology for all quality measures except CMS PSI-90; CQS baselines calculated using a rolling window of historical performance data that updates annually rather than remaining fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: allows baselines to evolve with improvements in care delivery, provides responsive quality assessment, aligns with target price baseline approach, and maintains stability by using historical (not contemporaneous) data in most instances. CMS proposes implementing this beginning in TEAM PY1 but seeks comment on beginning in PY2 to reduce implementation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: CQS baseline period alignment (July–June vs calendar year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to update baseline periods from a calendar year to a July to June period for the Hybrid HWR, CMS PSI-90, THA/TKA PRO-PM, and ISCMR measures to align with Hospital IQR and HAC program measurement timeframes; Hospital Harm measures and Information Transfer PRO-PM would continue to use calendar year baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment ensures consistency with existing programs, leverages validated data already collected on those timeframes, reduces participant confusion, and avoids operational challenges of recalc'ing measures solely for TEAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent CQS baseline methodology (alternative considered)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rolling concurrent CQS baseline would construct the national distribution of measure performance scores from the same performance-year data (i.e., contemporaneous baseline), recalculating benchmarks annually using the performance-year data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pros: captures real-time performance and methodological alignment for measures recalibrated annually. Cons: introduces uncertainty because final baseline calculations (percentile thresholds, scaling parameters) would not be available until after the measurement period concludes, reducing advance predictability for participants. CMS is not proposing this now but seeks comment on its possible adoption and timing (PY1 vs PY2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed historical CQS baseline with updated timeframes (alternative considered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain fixed historical CQS baselines but change the baseline periods from calendar year to July–June for specified measures; under this alternative baselines would be established and then remain fixed for multiple performance years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pros: stable targets and certainty for participants, easier long-term tracking. Cons: baselines can become outdated, reduce incentives for continued improvement, cannot adjust for data anomalies, and may be inequitable over model duration. CMS considered this but prefers sliding historical baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of baseline methodology implementation (PY1 vs PY2)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes implementing the sliding historical CQS baseline methodology beginning with TEAM PY1 but considered an alternative to begin in TEAM PY2 to reduce operational risk at model launch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning in PY1 avoids mid-model change and provides consistent methodology across model duration; beginning in PY2 could reduce operational/implementation risk but would introduce a mid-model methodological transition and potential participant confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target price construction methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Target prices are calculated using 3 years of rolling baseline episode spending, prospectively trended forward with 2 additional historical years to the performance year, at the MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region level, with updates made using performance year data during reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark prices are calculated from capped and standardized spending in the most recent baseline year dollars for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region; preliminary target prices include a prospective trend factor and discount factor; reconciliation updates trend (subject to cap) and normalization factor (subject to cap) and adjust for participant's realized performance year case mix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode spending capping (99th percentile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Episode spending will be capped at the 99th percentile for each of the 29 MS-DRG/HCPCS episode types and 9 regions when computing benchmark prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capping at the 99th percentile is part of standardizing benchmark calculations to limit influence of extreme outliers; results in 261 benchmark prices (29 episode types × 9 regions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark price calculation population
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmark prices will be calculated using all hospitals in a region, regardless of TEAM participation status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures benchmarks reflect the broader regional population rather than only TEAM participants, supporting comparability and normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment factors and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk adjustment factors include age group, Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) count, beneficiary economic risk, episode category-specific HCC adjusters, and hospital-level adjusters including a hospital bed size factor and a safety net hospital factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk adjusters are calculated at the MS-DRG/HCPCS level using a weighted linear regression where baseline years are weighted (baseline year 1 at 17%, year 2 at 33%, year 3 at 50%). Risk adjustment factors will be fixed and applied at reconciliation based on realized case mix; adjustments will be made available prior to each performance year so participants can estimate episode-level target prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization factor calculation and cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalize target prices so the average of the total risk-adjusted preliminary target price does not exceed the average of the total non-risk adjusted preliminary target price; the final normalization factor is the mean of the benchmark price divided by the mean of the risk-adjusted benchmark price for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final normalization factor will be capped should this ratio exceed ±5 percent of the prospective normalization factor, as finalized in prior IPPS rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective trend factor cap at reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The final target prices will include a retrospective trend factor, which will be capped at being within 3 percent of the prospective trend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cap limits how much trend updates at reconciliation can change target prices relative to prospectively applied trend assumptions, per prior rulemaking.
